The following are ketone components in essential oils that generally do not present safety considerations when used topically, through diffusion and inhalation: menthone, verbenone, valeranone, vetivone, fenchone, piperitone, jasmone, and turmerone.

The ketones to be extra cautious with:

Carvone: (-)-carvone is suggested at 1% max to avoid skin sensitization, (-)-carvone is present in Spearmint.
Pulegone: found in Pennyroyal, Calamint and Buchu, and very small amounts in Peppermint, Cornmint and Palo Santo. (Tisserand and Young p.624) Oils high in pulegone is hepatotoxic and contraindicated during pregnancy.
Thujone: found in Western Red Cedar, Genipi, Wormwood, Thuja, Sage, and Mugwort, and small amounts in Blue Yarrow and Hyssop. (Tisserand and Young p.638) Thujone is found to be neurotoxic and hepatotoxic and contraindicated during pregnancy. Should not be taken internally. (Tisserand and Young p.639-640)
Pinocamphone and isopinocamphone, found in Hyssop, are considered neurotoxic and convulsant—too stimulating to the nervous systems of epileptics. Contraindicated during pregnancy in all routes. Limited topical use, and should not be taken internally. (Tisserand and Young p.621-622)
Preparations with camphor should not be placed into or near the noses of infants and young children. If ingested by infants or children, camphor is proven to be fatal (4 teaspoons). (Tisserand and Young p.514)
Camphor can cause convulsions either from oral ingestion or, more rarely, inhalation.
Camphor is an eye and mucous membrane irritant. (Tisserand and Young p.514)
Camphor has been linked with miscarriage, but only in almost fatal doses.
There is abundant evidence that moderate amounts of camphor are not fetotoxic or teratogenic, however, oils high in camphor such as Feverfew (44%), Ho Leaf ct. camphor (84%), and Spanish Lavender (Lavandula stoechas, 56%) should be avoided during pregnancy. (Tisserand and Young p.152)
Although camphor is a CNS stimulant, overdoses can cause CNS depression.
In order to avoid any toxicity from camphor, dermal application should be limited to a maximum of 4.6% of total camphor content. (Tisserand and Young p.516)
There is some concern for the liver when using ketones in high daily doses over the long term. They resist being metabolized by the liver, so they tend to accumulate.

AGP Notes:
Sesquiterpene-high oils tend to be energetically and emotionally grounding. They are heavier oils, and most often middle or base notes. While monoterpenes tend to be uplifting and energetic, sesquiterpenes tend to be calming and centering. Compare the aroma and energetic impact of Balsam Copaiba (almost all sesquiterpenes) to Orange (almost all monoterpenes).  The shelf life for these heavier oils is longer. Generally, oils very high in sesquiterpenes last 6–8 years or longer.

AGP Notes:
Monoterpene-rich oils tend to be uplifting and energetic. Many of them reduce stagnation, supporting movement or change in the body. They are made of up only 10 carbons and varying numbers of hydrogen so they are small molecules. This means they can penetrate the skin easily and quickly.

Most monoterpene-rich oils are top or middle notes that evaporate quickly. The aromas of oils that are made up primarily of monoterpenes are more sharp and singular than other oils that have two or more chemical families.

Most oils rich in monoterpene have an antiseptic effect.
Most oils rich in monoterpene can be helpful decongestants for the respiratory and the muscular system (depending on the specific monoterpene rich oil).
Some are decongestants for the muscular system, which simply means there is improved circulation and reduced stagnation.
Many monoterpene-rich oils are rubifacients and provide an analgesic effect where muscle pain and stiffness are present.
Many monoterpene rich oils are anti-inflammatory—see individual datasheets.
Some oils rich in monoterpenes have an antibacterial or antiviral effect.
Highly lipophilic and penetrate the tissues of the body easily (penetration enhancers).
Many oils rich in monoterpene are effective airborne deodorizers and purifiers.

• Respiratory pathologies,particularly when excess mucous is present(bronchitis,flu,coughs and colds, etc.)
• Congestive diseases of the venous system and lymphatic
